answer: Each agent posts a bond that is slashed if random audits expose collusion. A trellis of trust links discounts endorsements from identities that only vouch for one another; agents gain weight through varied tasks and attestations from independently bonded peers. A beacon can select tasks for audit, while a ripple of mutual endorsements alone earns no standing. To mount a sybil attack, an adversary must lock real capital in every identity and risk losing it, then spend time building credible, independent history.
